subject: Node-farm saturation & 5xx/429 bursts — Nimbus escalation
messages:
From: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@nimbus.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@nimbus.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T15:03:12Z
Subject: Sudden 5xx/429 burst impacting API (URGENT)

Marcus / Dev —

We just started seeing a large spike of 5xx and 429 responses across our production calls to your hosted inference endpoint (region us-west-2). Latency jumps to >2s for many requests, and our clients are retrying aggressively which looks like a retry spiral. Examples attached (nginx-5xx-sample.log).

Impacted routes: /v1/generate (large batch workloads), some streaming calls timing out. This started ~14:58 PT and is persistent for the last 5–10 minutes. We are getting 20–30% errors on p95 traffic.

We need immediate triage and a mitigation plan. Can you confirm whether this is capacity saturation on your side or something else? We are evaluating contingency plans but would prefer to keep traffic on Redwood.

Elena (ops) and I are available on this thread and on Slack (nimbus-ops).

Thanks,
Carlos
Senior SRE, Nimbus Systems
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@nimbus.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T15:07:20Z
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx/429 burst impacting API (URGENT)

Carlos —

Thanks for the quick ping and the log attachment. We’re on it. Initial ask: can you confirm the affected model (model id and pinned version) and whether these calls are coming from a dedicated pool or on our hosted multi-tenant tier?

Immediate steps we are spinning up now:
- Triage on the serving-side to check node saturation and autoscaler events.
- Pull pool-level metrics (GPU utilization, queue length, inflight requests) and correlate with your timestamps.
- If this is Dedicated, we’ll evaluate warm pool burst and temporary routing to a compatible variant.

I’ll share a short interim status within 15 minutes.

—Marcus
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@nimbus.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T15:15:45Z
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx/429 burst impacting API (URGENT)

Following up with what I’m seeing from telemetry:
- The customer is on a Dedicated pool (dedicated-pool-28).
- Around 14:55 PT we observe a rapid increase in queued requests and GPU utilization hitting sustained 98–100% on three worker nodes.
- Autoscaler attempted to provision additional nodes but nodes entered 'provisioning' state; there were delayed accelerator allocations in the cloud provider (quota-scheduling) and two new nodes failed to join due to driver boot errors.
- Error profile: internal 5xx from serving runtime (OOM & timeout) and 429s emitted by our dispatcher when queue depth exceeds threshold.

I’ve attached a snapshot (pool-metrics-2026-11-20.png) and the autoscaler events dump (autoscaler-events-2026-11-20.json). Initial hypothesis: pool saturation + autoscaler lag + a set of long-running requests leaking KV-cache and holding GPUs.

Immediate mitigation options (ranked):
1) Route a subset (10–20%) of the traffic to a hosted compatible model variant to reduce pressure on the Dedicated pool.
2) Force-evict oldest long-running inference sessions (graceful kill) on two nodes to free cache and reduce OOMs.
3) Temporarily raise dispatcher queue threshold and enable shed-mode for high-cost models.

I’ll take action (2) unless you want to go with (1) immediately; (1) requires customer consent to route off Dedicated.

—Dev
SRE, Serving Runtime

Evelyn — flagging for leadership: Nimbus is seeing a persistent customer-impacting surge and may request credits if we don’t stabilize within SLA window. Please advise on any immediate commercial concessions.

Carlos, we expect the first visible improvement in 3–7 minutes after evictions and routing changes. I’ll post updates here.

—Marcus

—Elena
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:12:03Z
Subject: Post-incident note & request for exec sync

Evelyn / Karthik —

Status summary (morning after):
- Cause: Dedicated pool (dedicated-pool-28) hit sustained saturation due to a combination of queued large-batched requests and a small number of long-running call patterns that pinned KV caches.
- Autoscaler lag: provider-side accelerator allocation delays + two driver boot failures caused provisioning to fail for ~6 minutes, during which dispatcher returned 429s and runtime emitted 5xx timeouts.
- Customer impact: Nimbus reported p95 latency >2s and 15–25% error rates at peak; they experienced client-side retry amplification.

Immediate follow-ups requested:
- Karthik: authorize one-time warm node reserve for the customer (3 nodes for 48 hours) to avoid cold-provisioning on high-load windows.
- Dev: prepare a targeted runtime patch to detect long-lived sessions and enforce an upper TTL on pinned KV-cache (postmortem fix).
- Evelyn: please propose commercial remediation (SLA credit or one-time free warm pool) — customer is asking for compensation given impact.

I’ll schedule an exec sync 11:00 PT to align on the customer ask and next actions.

—Marcus
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T11:47:03Z
Subject: Re: Post-incident note & request for exec sync

Ack — approved temporary warm reserve (3 nodes, 48 hours) and greenlight on expedited runtime TTL change as a high-priority patch. Evelyn: go ahead with negotiation for credit (recommend 5% of monthly committed spend or equivalent service days).

I want a short postmortem doc (Ops ticket OPS-1429) with timeline, root cause, and three concrete mitigations: warm reservations for heavy customers, autoscaler health checks / provider quota pre-warm, runtime TTL bounds for KV cache.

—Karthik
